rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns from the disbelievers’ ignorance to the Prophet as the foremost person of understanding; the Quran surpasses every admonisher and explains all things.
rows.anchor: منبها على أنهم لا يفهمون لسان القال فضلا عن لسان الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God places a veil filling the space between the Prophet and those who reject the afterlife; it prevents them from perceiving him as he truly is and is unseen except by whom God wills.
rows.anchor: عن أن يدركوك حق الإدراك على ما أنت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coverings keep them from understanding the Quran, while the heaviness in their ears blocks beneficial hearing through their limited perception, not any defect in its clarity; he links this to 2:7.
rows.anchor: بالقصور في إدراكهم لا في بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet mentions God alone in the Quran, they turn away from the idols and flee; نفورا intensifies the image as a verbal noun or can mean fleeing people.
rows.anchor: وحقق المعنى وصوره بما يزيد في بشاعته تنفيرا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نفورا is an emphatic verbal noun from a different form, or a plural like قاعد وقعود, making their retreat especially vivid.
rows.anchor: مصدر من غير اللفظ مؤكد لأنه محصل لمعناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across its ten root permutations, وقر turns on gathering: ear heaviness or deafness gathers and stills perception, while a burden gathers what it contains.
rows.anchor: عشر تدور على الجمع كما مضى في آخر يوسف وأول الحجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes وقر with fatḥa for ear heaviness or deafness from وقر with kasra for a load; related forms describe stillness, dignity, and gathered weight.
rows.anchor: في الأذن أو ذهاب السمع كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الوقير can mean a flock of sheep, lambs, a specified number of sheep, or a flock with its dog, shelter, and shepherd; the senses share the idea of gathering.
rows.anchor: القطيع من الغنم أو صغارها أو خمسمائة منها أو عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permutation روق first denotes a horn, explained through its gathered solidity and roundness, and also swimming or its action as a collected effort.
rows.anchor: ولأنه يجمع إقدام صاحبه وعزمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further روق forms range across lifespan, what pleases or delights, beauty, coverings and porticoes, a hunter’s hide, courage, leadership, pure water, bodily form, snakes, and disasters; he relates the senses to gathering.
rows.anchor: لأن الفكر يجمع الخواطر لأجله فلا يظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The قرو family includes pursuit and stabbing, troughs and vessels, land, palm bases, abundance, water sources, backs, habits, bodily ailments, buds, and gatherings; the author explains these through collection or containment.
rows.anchor: والقروك القصد والتتبع كالاقتراء والاستقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He postpones the rest of this lexical family to his discussion of بورقكم هذه in al-Kahf 18:19.
rows.anchor: وسيأتي إن شاء الله تعالى بقية المادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows that their intense listening is driven either by their ears and hearts or by a wish to catch a slip they can mock and use to deny the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أو بسببه من إرادة الوقوع على سقطة يجعلونها موضع تكذيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نجوى describes them whispering secrets to one another after turning away from proper listening.
rows.anchor: يتناجون بأن يرفع كل منهم سره على صاحبه بعد إعراضهم عن الاستماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers tell their followers that they follow only a man whose mind is confused, reaching the height of injustice in this accusation.
rows.anchor: فامتطوا في هذا الوصف ذروة الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their comparisons—calling the Prophet a sorcerer, poet, madman, and the like—are far from his true character and make them stray.
rows.anchor: التي هي أبعد شيء عن صفتك من قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having strayed, they cannot find a route to make a sound comparison or to establish their case in action; this shows they cannot withstand the Quran even with a specious argument.
rows.anchor: إلى إصابة المحن في مثل , أو إحكام الأمر في عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding warning recalls God’s command not to invent comparisons about Him, since He knows and people do not; the cited verse is 16:74.
rows.anchor: فلا تضربوا لله الأمثال إن الله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers deny resurrection despite acknowledging their original creation and seeing the dead earth revived; the question in إذا is governed by a verb from مبعوثون, since what follows إن cannot govern backward.
rows.anchor: لا يعمل فيما قبلها . فالمهنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رفاتا means broken fragments and dust; خلقا جديدا asks whether they will be brought back as a new creation.
rows.anchor: أي حطاما مكسرا مفتتا وغبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge to become stone, iron, or anything they deem harder to revive shows that God can transfer human clay’s distinctiveness through growth, life, and speech to any material.
rows.anchor: أي يعظم كبيرة { في صدوركم } عن قبول الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who originated them when they were nothing can restore them by the same power that accomplished their first creation.
rows.anchor: لم تكونوا شيئا يعيدكم بالقدرة التي ابتدأكم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers move their heads up and down in astonishment and mockery, treating their ignorance as if it were confident knowledge.
rows.anchor: يحركونها من شدة التعجب والاستهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نغض means moving the head up and down; they ask when resurrection will occur in mockery.
rows.anchor: تحريك بارتفاع وانخفاض { ويقولون } استهزاء : { متى هو }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to answer calmly and without irritation that it may be near, then the next verse states the appointed day.
rows.anchor: غير ممتعض بحالهم ولا ضيق بقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call may come through the trumpet or another herald, such as a summons to leave the graves for recompense; calling and responding may also metaphorically describe resurrection’s speed and ease or the gathering for judgment.
rows.anchor: يناديكم المنادي من قبله بالنفخة أو بغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Responding in praise signifies complete submission to God’s encompassing power and knowledge, with no failure; those raised affirm His perfection.
rows.anchor: بإحاطته سبحانه بكل شيء قدرة وعلما من غير تخلف أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will think they remained dead only briefly, either because of the terrors surrounding them or because they remain ignorant of reality, as they are now.
rows.anchor: التي أحاطت بكم والتي تستقبلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must use the wisest speech and counsel with opponents so zeal does not provoke further harm or conflict.
rows.anchor: نهاهم عن ذلك لئلا يقولوا ما يهيج شرا أو تثير ضرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s نزغ is a prick that incites, corrupts, and whispers; since people are fallible, it can lead them to ill-timed insults or self-praise and provoke discord.
rows.anchor: يوشك أن يأتوا بما لا يناسب الحال أو الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s enmity toward humanity is primordial and intrinsic, which explains why believers must guard their speech.
rows.anchor: إن الشيطان كان } أي في قديم الزمان وأصل الطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading explains that God may guide people toward good or lead them toward evil, prompting them to assess their own conduct and perhaps turn from corruption.
rows.anchor: بأن ييسر لكم أفعال الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers taking this verse as the reason to speak well: God knows each person’s eventual happiness or misery, so believers must not condemn opponents, stir resentment, or exceed the prescribed conduct while their endings remain unknown.
rows.anchor: ويجوز - وهو - عندي أحسن - أن تكون الآية استئنافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not appointed as their guardian or guarantor; he brings good news and warning, and should treat opponents gently while instructing his companions to do likewise.
rows.anchor: وإنما أرسلناك بشيرا ونذيرا فدارهم وأمر أصحابك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows all inhabitants of heaven and earth, their states, capacities, and lifespans because He created them and differentiated their natures and forms.
rows.anchor: لأنه هو الذي خلقهم وفاوت بينهم في أخلاقهم وهيئاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This complete knowledge explains why people must not reject Muhammad’s prophethood because he was an orphan or dismiss the hungry, poorly clothed companions.
rows.anchor: يتيم أبي طالب - على ما كانوا يقولون - نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge encompasses every person’s worth and proper rank, so human assumptions cannot limit whom He chooses to favor.
rows.anchor: بأحوالعم ومقاديرهم وآجالهم وما يستأهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preference among creatures is a fruit of deeds and giving each its due; it displays God’s wisdom, comprehensive knowledge, and perfect power.
rows.anchor: أن من أعظم ثمرات العمل التفضيل بإعطاء كل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explicitly favored some prophets over others, whether they were messengers or not; their varied ranks do not make any of them cease to be virtuous.
rows.anchor: بعد أن جعلنا الكل فضلاء لتقوى كل منهم وإحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David is especially apt here as founder of the Jerusalem sanctuary, recipient of softened iron, and a king marked by humility and weeping rather than worldly swagger.
rows.anchor: المؤسس للمسجد الأقصى الذي وقع الإسراء إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Zabur consists of exhortations opposing arrogance and commanding the best speech, sincerity, mindfulness, and excellence, fitting the themes of this surah.
rows.anchor: خص من بينهم داود عليه السلام بكتاب كله مواعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic distinction takes different forms: Abraham’s migration, Moses’ purification of the sanctuary, David’s building it, and Muhammad’s Night Journey, leadership of the prophets, and ascent.
rows.anchor: تارة بالهجرة إليه كإبراهيم عليه السلام وتارة بقصد تطهيره من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David and Solomon’s kingship and extensive dominion are included in the earlier statement that God favored some people over others, 17:21.
rows.anchor: بالملك وسعة الأمر فدخل في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet said David’s recitation was made easy: he had his mounts saddled and finished reading before they were ready.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Zabur explicitly mentions Hell and resurrection, including bodily resurrection, whereas the Torah lacks a clear resurrection account and mentions Hell only once.
rows.anchor: وأما الزبور فذكر فيه النار والهاوية والجحيم في غير موضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Psalm describes spirits leaving bodies, the dead returning to dust, and God’s spirit renewing creation and the earth, affirming resurrection after death.
rows.anchor: ترسل روحك فيخلقون , وتجدد وجه الأرض دفعة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another Psalm warns against relying on rulers or human beings, whose spirits depart and return to dust, linking resurrection and the end of earthly works to reliance on God.
rows.anchor: لا تتوكلوا على الرؤساء ولا على بني البشر الذين ليس عندهم خلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author anticipates Jewish interlocutors claiming there is no resurrection and notes their reported claim that their religion was better guided than Muhammad’s; he points to the Torah and Gospel context and al-Nisa 4:51.
rows.anchor: ودينكم خير من دين محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge addresses those who invoke beings such as angels, Ezra, Jesus, and idols, assuming that intermediaries can secure benefit or intercession with God.
rows.anchor: كالملائكه وعزير والمسيح والأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: None of these supposed deities can remove hardship or even transfer it to a milder state, much less replace it with good or divert it to an enemy; compare 25:19.
rows.anchor: له من حالة إلى ما هو أخف منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported occasion of revelation is Quraysh’s complaint about a drought after the Prophet prayed against them for seven years, like Joseph’s famine.
rows.anchor: شكوى قريش إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم ما نزل هم من القحط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording denies the false gods’ power in itself, so their incapacity does not depend on whether people invoke them.
rows.anchor: النفي مسبب عن الدعاء فيتقيد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The very beings worshipped as intermediaries seek nearness to God through righteous acts, hoping for mercy and fearing punishment; accountable beings do so actually, while idols are only objects of worship.
rows.anchor: المنزلة والدرجة والقربة بالأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that some humans worshipped jinn who later accepted Islam, while their human worshippers persisted in their old religion, showing the worshippers’ error.
rows.anchor: وروى البخاري في التفسير عن عبد الله رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking closeness to God means competing in righteous deeds for the nearest rank, while hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment.
rows.anchor: يتسابقون بالأعمال مسابقة من يطلب كل منهم أن يكون إليه أقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s punishment deserves caution from everyone, even a near angel or sent prophet, given the destruction witnessed among earlier generations; God has spared this community total extermination.
rows.anchor: جديرا بأن يحذر لكل أحد من ملك مقرب ونبي مرسل فضلا عن غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every town will either be destroyed before the Resurrection or suffer severe punishment while remaining; Jerusalem was twice punished for corruption, as recounted earlier in 17:4 and 17:7.
rows.anchor: من القرى هذه التي أنتم بها وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This fate is written in God’s book as a fixed report, not a decree subject to abrogation.
rows.anchor: على وجه الخبر , والأخبار لا تنسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning includes hiding the opponents after their long security and destroying their dignitaries through the solitary man they despise, then bringing him into Mecca with a powerful army.
rows.anchor: أن ندخله إلى بلدكم هذا بجنود أولي بأس شديد

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: A report on future city ruins traces a sequence from Armenia to Egypt to Kufa, then describes wider regional destruction and the conquest of Constantinople by a Hashimite.
rows.anchor: الجزيرة آمنة من الخراب حتى تخرب إرمينية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet’s statement that Medina will be the last town among the Muslim towns to be ruined; al-Tirmidhi also transmitted it by this route.
rows.anchor: آخر قرية من قرى الإسلام خرابا المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God was not prevented from sending signs cannot mean inability, which would imply that an omnipotent agent is unable to act; rather it reflects His knowledge of the outcome.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أخذه على ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples rejected requested signs and were destroyed; God knows Quraysh’s doomed members would likewise call them magic, while delaying punishment preserves future descendants and honors this community.
rows.anchor: أن هؤلاء مثل الأولين في أن الشقي منهم لا يؤمن بالمقترحات كما لم يؤمن بغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The she-camel was a bright, unmistakable sign that should have made witnesses discern the truth, yet the Thamud wronged themselves by refusing belief and fear.
rows.anchor: جديرة بأن يستبصر بها كل من شاهدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud is singled out because they were Arabs, Quraysh knew their story, and their nearby dwellings made their fate a familiar warning.
rows.anchor: خص آية ثمود بالذكر تحذيرا بسبب أنهم عرب اقترحوا ما كان سببا لاستئصالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel emerging from stone illustrates the power to recreate even stone or iron; the interwoven mention of David points to iron and the camel to stone.
rows.anchor: لأنها حيوان أخرجه من حجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order of David and the she-camel makes a deliberately crossed correspondence: David evokes iron and the camel evokes stone.
rows.anchor: والناقة إشارة إلى الحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends signs, whether requested or not, only as warnings: those who fear are saved, while those who do not fear perish.
rows.anchor: أي للمرسل إليهم بها , فإن خافوا نجوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He recalls that people already destined not to believe will reject every sign, as stated in Yunus 10:96.
rows.anchor: الذين حقت عليهم كلمت ربك لا يؤمنون ولو جاءتهم كل ءاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s encompassing knowledge and power also mean He protects the Prophet from opponents and will make his religion prevail.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه مانعك منهم وحائطك ومظهر دينك كما وعدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Night Journey vision tested people and established proof in the visible world; it was not meant to convert those already destined for disbelief or to add to God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: لا ليؤمن أحد من حقت عليهم الكلمة ولا لنزداد نحن علما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Isra was a waking bodily journey to Jerusalem and the heavens, the position of the majority and Sunnis; widespread denial and apostasy prove it was no ordinary dream, while its possibility follows from God’s power.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب الجمهور وأهل السنة والجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term رؤيا can be a metaphor for a waking event because its extraordinary wonders resemble what normally occurs in dreams; an ordinary dream would not have become a public trial.
rows.anchor: وهي للمنام - على وجه التشبيه والاستعارة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the vision God showed the Prophet was an actual sight with his eyes on the Night Journey.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cursed tree is Zaqqūm, cursed because it is harmful and located in the abode of curse; like the Night Journey, it tests people and establishes proof about belief and disbelief.
rows.anchor: العرب تسمي كل ضار ملعونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their objection that fire consumes trees ignores that God can make a tree grow in fire just as He produces fire from green wood.
rows.anchor: أن الذي جعل لهم من الشجر الأخضر نارا قادر على أن يجعل في النار شجرا

rows.speaker: زين الدين أبو بكر بن الحسين المراغي
rows.claim: A Medina history recounts that the 654 AH al-Harra fire advanced for three months, consuming hills and stones but sparing trees, illustrating an extraordinary fire’s behavior.
rows.anchor: تأكل ما مرت عليه من جبل وحجر ولا تأكل الشجر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The author cites a Prophetic prediction that a fire would emerge from the Hijaz and light the necks of camels at Busra.
rows.anchor: لا تقوم الساعة حتى تخرج نار بالحجار تضيء لها أعناق الإبل ببصرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the challenge about decayed bodies, Adam’s creation from inert clay and immediate bestowal of living speech is an even greater demonstration of God’s power to recreate.
rows.anchor: وذلك بخلق آدم عليه السلام الذي هو أصلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s story consoles the Prophet that signs do not help those decreed for misery; even God’s chosen first prophet suffered greatly from an envious opponent, and envy drives much rebellion.
rows.anchor: بأن الآيات لا تنفع المحكوم بشقاوته وبأن آدم عليه السلام قد سلط عليه الحاسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, and they obeyed; Iblis refused despite knowing God’s signs and greatness, because he was among those decreed for misery.
rows.anchor: أبى أن يسجد لكونه ممن حقت عليه الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s claim that fire is nobler than clay accuses God of injustice and ignores clay’s greater usefulness; all substances share one kind, and God alone grants distinctions, as in 17:55.
rows.anchor: فإن الجواهر كلها من جنس واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s question asks why the weak human God honored should outrank him, the stronger one; the author presents it as an extreme breach of etiquette.
rows.anchor: بم كرمته علي مع ضعفه وقوتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis swears that if granted life until the Resurrection, he will dominate Adam’s descendants through seduction, except for a few protected allies of God.
rows.anchor: كما يستولي الآكل على ما أخذه في حنكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s command to go permits Iblis to pursue his declared course by divine will, not command; neither he nor his followers can exceed God’s decree concerning their misery.
rows.anchor: فإنك لن تعدوا أمرنا فيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bare verb in فمن تبعك may suggest that those who follow Satan from their original disposition, without being worked on, are deeply rooted in evil.
rows.anchor: أن من تبعه بغير معالجة من فطرته الأولى لا يكون إلا عريقا في الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is the complete, sufficient recompense for Satan and everyone who follows him, commensurate with their evil deeds.
rows.anchor: مكملا وافيا بما تستحقون على أعمالكم الخبيثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifteen permutations of وفر revolve around breadth, exceeding a limit, and surplus; وفر itself can indicate a large place, intact hide, ear-length hair, a meter, wealth, or abundance.
rows.anchor: تدور على السعة , والمجاوزة للحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ورف derivatives describe freshness and extent: lush growth, broad or lengthening shade, swollen or extended tissue, and a bright appearance filling the eye.
rows.anchor: ورف النبت يرف إذا رأيت له بهجة من ريه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فور forms evoke overflow and expansion: boiling that spills over, swelling veins, spreading scent, quick movement, and energetic animals or offspring.
rows.anchor: وفارت القدر - إذا غلت حتة يعلو ما فيها فتفيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فرو and related forms include garments, scalp, barren land, wealth, gathered vegetation, and other ample coverings or possessions, which the author relates to surplus and breadth.
rows.anchor: والفروة : الأرض البيضاء ليس لها نبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رفا means repairing and joining cloth or bringing people together, as in a wedding blessing; related forms quiet a frightened person and express mercy or compassion.
rows.anchor: والرفاء - ككساء : الالتحام والاجتماع والاتفاق
